audience: IT and finance teams: traceable project cost visibility and owned invoice-exception follow-up.
sources: Invented project and supplier master data; not a confirmed customer system.
Invented approved cost budgets, actual-cost postings and AP snapshots; no customer records.
Generated calendar and cost classification supporting consistent financial comparisons.

research.notes: Fictional regression example, not researched customer data or deployment approval.

proposal.title: Project Finance Control Tower
proposal.business_question: Which fictional projects are over their approved cost budgets for selected complete months, and which related supplier invoices on hold need finance follow-up?
proposal.audience_rationale: Finance sees reconciled cost-to-budget measures and invoice exceptions; IT sees consistent definitions and illustrative lineage across synthetic source families.
proposal.decision: Record an owned project or supplier follow-up in a separate action database; never modify accounting records.
assumptions: All projects, suppliers, records, financial patterns and exceptions are fictional; no actual customer performance or source schema is implied.
Illustrative USD amounts are stored as integer cents; no tax, foreign exchange, revenue recognition or profit-margin calculation.
Positive cost variance means actual cost exceeds approved budget; it is not forecast cost-to-complete.
Each project/category/month has one approved budget. Actual postings split a deliberately selected 85%-140% budget factor exactly, using integer arithmetic, with 2 or 3 postings per budget cell.
Invoice balances are a snapshot as of 2026-10-31. Invoice-date filters select cohorts, not historical AP balances. Holds do not imply a cause of budget variance.
Do not add invoice balances to actual costs, assume production source contents, or claim production lineage from synthetic metadata.
Budget and actual comparisons require complete calendar months, not arbitrary day filters. Fiscal calendar and customer currency remain unconfirmed.
Raw Files and staging copies are small synthetic artifacts, not a migration or performance benchmark.

reporting.notes: Use complete-calendar-month period slicers. Budget dates are month starts; do not compare a daily actual subset with an entire monthly budget. Use single-direction dim_period -> dim_date -> facts, project -> facts, cost category -> budget/actual, supplier -> invoices. Supplier filters do not apply to cost-to-budget measures: keep invoice and cost visuals separately scoped. Invoice balances are fixed as of 2026-10-31, not historical balances. Q3 2026 is fully covered; Q4 2025 and Q4 2026 are incomplete and must be labelled. Ratios are fractions formatted as percentages; recompute after aggregating their components.

tables.name: dim_project

columns.name: cost_factor_bps
columns.description: Synthetic scenario parameter only; 10000 means actual equals budget, not an observed business attribute

columns.name: calendar_year

tables.name: bronze_budget
tables.grain: One project x cost category x calendar month
tables.purpose: Simulated approved-cost-budget extract and raw JSON landing

columns.name: budget_month_start
columns.description: Budget month start; related to shared daily calendar

columns.name: approved_budget_cents
columns.description: Illustrative approved monthly cost budget in cents

columns.name: cost_factor_bps
columns.description: Synthetic allocation parameter inherited from project, not a financial measure

tables.name: bronze_cost_posting
tables.purpose: Simulated postings with exact budget-dependent allocation

columns.name: budget_id
columns.description: Synthetic allocation lineage to staging; do not create a fact-to-fact model relationship

columns.name: project_id
columns.description: Conformed project copied from the same budget cell

columns.name: cost_category_id
columns.description: Conformed category copied from the same budget cell

columns.name: posting_date
columns.description: Posting within the budget month; first 28 days deliberately avoid month rollover

columns.name: actual_cost_cents
columns.description: Exact allocated actual cents; children sum to floor(budget * cost_factor_bps / 10000)

columns.name: hold_reason

tables.name: silver_supplier_invoice
tables.purpose: Typed invoice records and consistent balances

metrics.name: approved_budget_cents
metrics.label: Approved cost budget
metrics.interpretation: Approved monthly cost budget; use complete month filters and conformed project/category keys.

metrics.name: actual_cost_cents
metrics.label: Actual cost
metrics.interpretation: Actual postings; aggregate independently of budgets and invoices before comparison.

metrics.name: held_invoice_count
metrics.label: Held supplier invoices
metrics.interpretation: Held invoices with positive current open balance as of 2026-10-31; selected months identify invoice cohorts.

metrics.name: held_open_balance_cents
metrics.label: Held invoice open balance
metrics.interpretation: Current held open balance as of 2026-10-31, not historical AP, cash forecast or additional cost.

derived_metrics.name: cost_variance_cents
derived_metrics.label: Cost over budget
derived_metrics.interpretation: Actual minus budget at identical project/category/month grain; positive means over budget. Missing operands remain null.

derived_metrics.name: cost_variance_ratio
derived_metrics.label: Cost variance percentage
derived_metrics.interpretation: Aggregated variance / aggregated budget; 0.10 means 10%. Recalculate after aggregation, never average row percentages. Missing or zero-budget comparisons remain null.
